A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. v2 retains Appendices A–G and adds H–I; renumbering and relocation can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training, payload-recoverability, generalization, text-quality and linear-probe experiments, including an XOR-masking control.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds capability benchmarks, mixed-motive training, temperature robustness and retokenization results.

M1.justification: Section 6.5 introduces a mixed-motive training variant combining 75% steganographic examples with 25% ordinary instruction-tuning examples. This adapts the training procedure to preserve capabilities; the geometric encoding, bucketing, model architectures and probe methods remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds downstream knowledge and commonsense evaluation on MMLU, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and WinoGrande, substantially extending coverage beyond secret transmission and detection. WikiText-103, helpful-instructions and Alpaca remain; mixed-motive training reuses the existing helpful-instructions source.

E2.justification: ASCII+Parity remains the attack baseline, and the same four encoding/bucketing combinations and base-model probe references are retained. The added studies reuse these comparison methods under new training and evaluation conditions.

E3.justification: v2 adds the 75/25 training mixture, capability degradation averaged across four benchmarks, and matched single-objective versus mixed-motive evaluations. Appendix H adds temperature 0.0 versus 0.7 testing and tokenization/decode/retokenization measurements across three text segments. Existing Wiki/TrojanStego hyperparameters and probe protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether benign instruction data mitigates capability loss, whether probe detection survives mixed-motive training, and whether sampling or retokenization disrupts transmission. These address substantial practical robustness questions absent from v1. The original OOD and XOR controls remain.

E5.justification: Appendix H.1 explicitly reports averaging three runs of 2,000 samples for the new temperature experiment. Existing classifier seeds, text-quality SEM reporting and probe confidence intervals remain unchanged. No increase in runs for retained experiments or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: Original scores are retained, while Table 1 adds mixed-motive results, Table 3 adds capability losses, Figure 6 adds probe results, and Tables 7–8 add robustness outcomes. For example, v2 reports Llama-LoRA A+E exact match of 38% under mixed training versus the retained 30% under single-objective training, and Llama WikiText bucket-flip rates of 7.32% for parity versus 0.45% for embedding bucketing.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, the geometric constructions, Theorems 7.1–7.2 and their Appendix B proofs are unchanged. The added robustness and scaling discussions introduce no new formal derivation or theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about lower recoverability, improved secret encoding and mechanistic detection. The new experiments support and qualify these claims without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes acceptable text quality from retained downstream capability and interprets mixed training as a partial mitigation. Appendices H–I add sampling and retokenization explanations and substantive limits involving exposure conditions, payload size, symbolic tasks and alphabet-search scaling. The hidden-state-access limitation was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents the mixed-training ratio, instruction-data source and reuse of Appendix D hyperparameters. Appendix H explicitly identifies greedy decoding as the main evaluation default and describes the retokenization pipeline. Existing implementation details and future code-release commitments are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the benchmark references for MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag and WinoGrande. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to TrojanStego, inference-time steganography and mechanistic detection remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative gains Sections 6.5 and 7.4 and Appendices H–I, with limited edits to the XOR discussion, impact statement and terminology. Most existing prose and section order remain intact; the first-page publication footer also changes.

P2.justification: The evidence displays expand substantially: Table 1 gains mixed-motive rows and highlighting, Table 3 presents capability comparisons, Figure 6 presents mixed-motive probes, and Tables 7–8 present robustness results. Existing displays are retained and reflowed; the XOR table becomes Table 4, and Figure 5 only changes some TS labels to T.

improvement.justification: v1 assessed text quality without measuring retained downstream capabilities. v2 addresses this important gap through capability benchmarks, a mixed-motive mitigation and verification that probe detection survives it (Sections 6.5 and 7.4). Appendix I also supplies meaningful applicability limits. The gains are substantial, although Table 7 needs correction: its near-invariant bit-accuracy claim conflicts with the Ministral Full E+E row's 3.1-point drop, and that row reports exact match exceeding bit accuracy. These localized inconsistencies weaken the temperature analysis but do not outweigh the broader validation gains.
